messages:
aria: quick ask — we need a small matrix of overhead numbers for the release toggle: streaming on vs off, and function/tool-calling path vs plain generation. can someone run a quick smoke benchmark today?

devin: I can take the streaming vs non-streaming runs. what model + seq length do you want?

aria: thanks. target model = redwood-3b-v2 (prod-serving), seq = 512 prompt + 256 gen (so ~768 total). aim for p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec. small runs are fine (1k calls) but include warmup.

leila: for function calling, do you want the full JSON parse step included (i.e., structured output -> serializer -> parsing latency) or just end-to-end as seen by the client?

aria: end-to-end as seen by client. include two tool-call variants: 1) simple tool call (single function schema) 2) nested tool chain (2 calls). both streaming and non-streaming.

devin: copying the bench command I'll use for reproducibility:

```
# run from perf box
bench-runner --target api \
  --model redwood-3b-v2 \
  --seq 768 \
  --concurrency 8 \
  --requests 1000 \
  --modes non-streaming,streaming \
  --workloads "plain,func-simple,func-nested" \
  --warmup 100 \
  --output /tmp/bench-1772356789.json
```

devin: note: include header X-Redwood-Route: public-default to hit the hosted route. also set CACHE=off env to avoid prefix cache influence for these numbers.

aria: perfect. can you also capture a cpu/gpu flame or perf trace for one representative run? just one streaming and one non-streaming sample is enough.

sam.k: I'll validate the function-call schemas and provide a small prompt corpus. pushing PR with prompts now — PR #1428.

leila: small nit — for nested tool chain specify a 2-step: step1 returns small json, step2 consumes it. we should record parse+validation time separately if possible.

devin: got it. running now. ETA ~45m. I'll drop the summary here.

perf-bot: automated run finished (prelim). results attached: 
- plain non-streaming: p50=120ms p95=260ms tokens/s=95 
- plain streaming: p50=130ms p95=300ms tokens/s=88 
- func-simple non-streaming: p50=150ms p95=340ms tokens/s=82 
- func-simple streaming: p50=165ms p95=380ms tokens/s=76 
- func-nested non-streaming: p50=210ms p95=500ms tokens/s=60 
- func-nested streaming: p50=230ms p95=560ms tokens/s=55

perf-bot: trace links: https://perf.internal/runs/1772356789/streaming-sample and https://perf.internal/runs/1772356789/nonstream-sample

aria: awesome — that matches my expectations (streaming + function calls add ~10-20% latency overhead, nested calls worse). can you annotate which portion is serialization / http framing vs model decode?

devin: early look at traces: ~40% of extra time in function paths is spend in JSON serialization/parsing + our schema validator. model decode delta is small (~5-8% increased token time in streaming due to framing). attaching flame snippet:

```
# simplified flame (percent of extra time)
json/serialize: 42%
validator/schema: 18%
http/frame/flush: 15%
model/decode: 8%
other: 17%
```

leila: okay, action items:
- devin: can we try a variant where we do minimal validation (skip deep schema) to see wins?
- sam.k: reduce response object size for nested steps (trim keys) and re-run sample.
- infra: can we test increasing http flush buffer for streaming to reduce syscalls? @ops-bot can you help?

ops-bot: noted. will test altering flush interval and report back in ~2 hours.

devin: running a quick variant with validator disabled now. early numbers look promising: func-nested streaming p95 down from 560ms -> 420ms. tokens/s up ~10%.

aria: great signal. let's capture a follow-up run in the same thread with validator disabled and trimmed payload. if still good, propose lib change for light-validator as opt-in for low-latency endpoints.

sam.k: PR #1429 with trimmed payloads and example minimal serializer. cc @leila for review.

devin: summary will include csv with columns: mode, workload, p50, p95, tokens/s, notes. I'll post by EOD. :thumbsup:

aria: thanks everyone. if anyone else wants to run different concurrency/seq combos, add to this thread. otherwise we'll use these as the basis for the release note and perf guardrails.

leila: thanks — bookmarking traces and PRs.

aria: closing loop — postmortem-lite: streaming adds small framing cost, function schema/validation dominates overhead for nested tool-chains. next steps listed above.
